posts.title: An Artist’s Interpretation
posts.description: In the summer of 1977—shortly after Star Wars’s release—my family moved to Eureka, Illinois, where my father had accepted a faculty appointment at tiny Eureka College. posts.title: I met a traveller from an antique land
posts.description: My undergraduate degree was in studio art, with a concentration in printmaking, and my favorite professor was the late great Garret Boone, or “Reverend Boone” as his students knew him (he was not ordained). I only had him officially for one class, Sculpture 101, but I worked with him on and off on various projects … Continue reading "I met a traveller from an antique land"

posts.title: The days dwindle down to a precious few
posts.description: My high school girlfriend was named Angie, and she had a great singing voice. I mean, I assume she still does; the last I heard she was a high school choral teacher. Anyway, I remember that I used to bug her (what a great boyfriend I was) by serenading the Rolling Stones’ “Angie” to her. … Continue reading "The days dwindle down to a precious few"
